decisions.reason: The bowl-clearance constraint is owned by the source Requirement and does not alter the whisk configuration attributes. The separate whisk-positioning clause from the same message is already represented in this candidate's existing MODIFY.
Easy bowl removal without whisk or motor interference does not change splash-control state. The message's splash guidance reiterates the existing target and mitigation options.
The new bowl-removal clearance constraint does not change the required foam quality, texture, or high-speed mixing behavior.
The source requires unobstructed bowl removal but does not change bowl capacity, depth, or the accepted size reference.
Bowl-removal clearance does not alter the dispensing valve, flow behavior, dispensing drive, or operating sequence.
The source adds a mechanical removal-clearance constraint and does not modify either existing liquid-containment requirement.
The source does not change the BOM deliverable or component-selection goal; any later design implementation belongs to execution or artifact work rather than a propagated state change.
The clearance requirement does not change the V1 priority or the current custom-spout sourcing policy.

Although the client frames the constraint as input to layout refinement, the system-layout deliverable and selected design direction remain unchanged; duplicating the product constraint into the artifact Requirement is unnecessary.
The mechanical bowl-clearance decision has no effect on the beige and green color scheme.
The bowl-removal constraint does not alter the machine name, wording, or placard placement.
The required bowl clearance does not change the DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity.
